title: Route/Model/Customer Economic Fingerprint Service
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build a streaming-first service that produces a compact, auditable economic fingerprint for every request pipeline slice: per-route, per-model-variant, and per-customer. The fingerprint is a normalized breakdown of cost and latency components (ingress queueing, batching wait, model compute, KV cache effect, serialization/post-processing, egress/network) plus metadata (route, model_variant, plan_tier, customer_id, request_size, token_breakdown). This will be the canonical source for the Console cost/latency breakdown dashboards and will feed the chargeback and billing insights pipelines.
acceptance_criteria:
1) For a nightly test corpus of 200k requests we produce fingerprints with per-component totals that sum to observed cost within <=3% drift.
2) Streaming pipeline runs with end-to-end latency < 90s for 99% of events at expected load (2k reqs/s).
3) Console dashboards show per-route/per-customer breakdown derived from fingerprints and match spot-check replay results.
4) Audit records retained in S3 for 90 days and queryable for forensic replay.
5) Feature-flagged rollout with ability to fallback to existing Aggregator v1 without data loss.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach: enrich ingress request events (route + request_id + token counts) with runtime traces (compute_start/compute_end, batch_id, model_variant, hardware) and low-cardinality telemetry (KV cache hit samples, batching stats). Join streams on request_id in a Beam/Flink streaming job that performs per-request attribution logic and emits compact fingerprints to ClickHouse and raw JSON to S3 for audit.
Attribution rules: token-level compute cost estimated via model_variant profiles (tokens * per_token_time * device_cost). Shared batch overhead apportioned by effective compute share heuristics (per-token compute time within batch). KV cache benefits recorded as a negative compute delta and flagged with sampling rate to enable extrapolation.
Store schema: time, request_id, route, model_variant, customer_id, tokens_total, tokens_cached, compute_ms, compute_cost_usd, queue_ms, serialization_ms, network_ms, total_cost_usd, shard_key.
We will implement an offline validation job that replays raw traces to verify streaming attributions within tolerance before enabling production rollouts.
data_schema: Fields (flat): event_time, request_id, route_id, model_variant, customer_id, plan_tier, tokens_prompt, tokens_generated, tokens_cached, batch_id, device_type, compute_ms, queue_ms, serialization_ms, egress_ms, compute_cost_usd, network_cost_usd, storage_cost_usd, total_cost_usd, fingerprint_version, sample_rate, provenance_link
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in): run streaming job in shadow mode and emit fingerprints to a 'staging.fingerprints' ClickHouse table and S3 prefix. Phase 2 (read-only): Console reads staging table behind feature flag; compare dashboard numbers with Aggregator v1 for two weeks. Phase 3 (opt-in write): enable downstream consumers to read production fingerprints but keep billing on old ledger. Phase 4 (switch): switch chargeback pipelines to new fingerprints and deprecate v1. Each phase gated by observed reconciliation metrics and sign-off from Finance and PM.
test_plan:
Unit tests for attribution math, integration tests with local ClickHouse, end-to-end replay test using synthetic traces (golden dataset). Load test to validate 2k req/s sustained with spikes to 10k req/s. Accuracy test: replay sampled real traffic and compare to model-instrumented ground truth; require <=5% deviation per-component for median and <=10% for 99th.
Automated alerts: drift > 5% vs nightly replay triggers autosuspend of write mode.
risks_and_mitigations:
1) Risk: attribution in shared batches is approximate and could bias high-volume tenants. Mitigation: expose per-batch deterministic apportionment and provide reconciliation tooling to recompute per-tenant costs offline if needed.
2) Risk: KV cache sampling may undercount benefits. Mitigation: increase sampling on suspect routes and backfill with offline replays for high-value customers.
3) Risk: ClickHouse partition churn from high-card routes. Mitigation: use daily partitions with route bucketing and high-cardinality encode (string interning).
4) Risk: E2E pipeline latency spikes during incidents. Mitigation: graceful degradation: emit a compact minimal fingerprint (aggregate cost+latency) when enrichment joins time out.
